claims.claim: A recurrent network applies a shared transition repeatedly over time and passes hidden state between steps.
claims.notes: The article states batch/time/feature shapes separately.

claims.claim: Backpropagation through time multiplies local state Jacobians, which can lead to vanishing or exploding gradients.
claims.notes: Gradient clipping limits norm but does not restore information already lost.

claims.claim: The 1997 LSTM paper introduced a constant-error-flow memory path with multiplicative gates; the commonly shown forget gate belongs to later LSTM variants.
claims.notes: The article distinguishes original LSTM from the later forget-gate formulation.

claims.claim: The forget gate was introduced in later LSTM work, including Gers, Schmidhuber and Cummins (2000).
claims.notes: Modern four-gate equations are labeled as modern/common formulation.

claims.claim: GRU combines reset and update gating with a candidate state; exact update-gate conventions vary across notation and implementations.
claims.notes: The article states the chosen convention explicitly.

claims.claim: Additive attention computes a compatibility score between decoder state and each encoder state, normalizes scores and forms a weighted context vector.
claims.notes: Attention weights are not treated as causal explanations.

claims.claim: Transformer training can process positions in parallel, while standard autoregressive decoding remains token-by-token and full attention forms a sequence-length-squared interaction matrix.
claims.notes: The article avoids claiming that Transformer generation is fully parallel.
